problem: Language-guided robotics is hard because of limited training data, multiple levels of reasoning, and multi-dimensional continuous action spaces.
motivation: Progress in vision, NLP and robotics suggests they can be combined so robots follow operator instructions. The thesis splits the problem into vision-and-language navigation (VLN) and vision-and-language manipulation to tackle each challenge.
key_idea: Use a large-scale pre-training dataset (BnB), hierarchical Transformer encoders, and a Transformer that predicts continuous multi-dimensional actions for language-guided navigation and tabletop manipulation.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablations or analysis are visible. The abstract claims data scarcity is addressed by pre-training on BnB, and that hierarchical encoding and continuous action prediction help.
method: BnB dataset pre-training: efficient pre-training procedure for VLN using the new BnB dataset to address data scarcity
Hierarchical Transformer: encodes several levels of abstraction for navigation
Continuous multi-dimensional action prediction: Transformer-based method for tabletop manipulation tasks
